policy_text:
Harrow Vale Equipment Permit Office: heavy equipment operating permits.
R1. A permit is approved when R2, R3, R4 and R5 all pass, and denied when any of them fails.
R2. The operator must hold a current Vale operator certificate.
R3. Proof of insurance must be on file, unless the equipment is class A.
R4. In a residential zone, the equipment's noise rating must be 70 dB or lower. Outside residential zones this rule does not apply.
R5. Night operation is not permitted in a residential zone. Outside residential zones this rule does not apply.
R6. If the case does not say whether proof of insurance is on file, assume it is on file.
R7. Equipment painted heritage green receives a commemorative decal. This does not affect the permit decision.
R8. If a fact needed by R2-R5 is not stated and no rule supplies a default, the decision is cannot determine.
case_text: Dara Okonkwo applied on behalf of Fenwick Earthworks to run a class B tracked excavator at the old grain depot on Mill Road, a lot zoned industrial. The machine is painted heritage green, a holdover from the depot's previous owner. Dara attached a current Vale operator certificate for the driver, Tomas Reyes, and the clerk confirmed that proof of insurance is on file. The excavator's noise rating is 85 dB. Work is scheduled for daytime hours only, 7 a.m. to 4 p.m., over three weeks while the depot's foundations are cleared.

policy_text:
Orrin Foundation Small Grants Program.
R1. A grant is approved when R2, R3, R4 and R5 all pass, and denied when any of them fails.
R2. The applicant must be a registered nonprofit, unless the applicant is an individual artist with at least 2 letters of support.
R3. The requested amount must be 20,000 credits or less.
R4. The applicant must have no overdue report from a prior Orrin grant. If the case does not mention prior reports, assume there is no overdue report.
R5. The project must take place within the Orrin river districts.
R6. Applicants founded more than 50 years ago are listed on the Foundation's honor roll. This does not affect the grant decision.
R7. If a fact needed by R2-R5 is not stated and no rule supplies a default, the decision is cannot determine.
case_text: The Lantern Street Reading Circle, a registered nonprofit founded 12 years ago, requests 15,000 credits to run weekly literacy evenings at the Eastbank library, inside the Orrin river districts. The application includes 1 letter of support from the library director. The Circle completed an Orrin grant two years ago and filed its final report on time, so it has no overdue reports. The coordinator, Mei Lindqvist, plans to buy chairs, lamps and a year of tea.
